passage: I've lived next door to Leela since we were six, so I know her family well. I'm Zainab. Her father is proud of her, really proud. Every test mark goes onto the family group within minutes. At dinner the talk is ranks, olympiads, which coaching batch next. When she got 94 in maths, he asked, "Who got the extra marks?" Last month on the terrace, Leela said, very quietly, "If I stop being clever, I think they'd stop liking me." I didn't know what to say. I just sat next to her. Then something changed. Her aunt must have said something. On Sunday I heard her father through the wall asking Leela to teach him the song she'd been humming. No marks, just singing badly together. Leela was laughing, properly laughing.

qa.q: Where does Leela's father post every test mark?
qa.a: Onto the family group within minutes.

qa.q: What was Leela afraid of, based on what she said on the terrace?
qa.a: She was afraid her family would stop liking her if she stopped being clever.

qa.q: What small change seemed to help Leela at home?
qa.a: Her father spent time singing with her with no talk of marks, showing interest in her beyond her ability.

qa.q: How does Zainab seem to feel watching Leela's situation?
qa.a: Zainab seems worried and unsure what to say, but stays close, and is glad to hear Leela laughing on Sunday.

grounding: A neighbour sees a gifted girl whose proud father pushes constant achievement until she feels loved only for being clever, and how valuing her beyond ability helps.

passage: Saturday. At his cousin's wedding, Yogesh put an arm around Gopika and told every uncle, "Our genius. Ninety-eight in science!" Gopika smiled until her cheeks hurt. Wednesday. The results came. Second rank. She went straight to the bathroom and cried with the tap running. When she came out she asked, "Papa, would you still love me if I was just ordinary?" Yogesh stared at her. He didn't answer. He hadn't known she thought that. The next Sunday. He took her for cutting chai at the corner stall. "I watched you with your little cousin at the wedding," he said. "You carried her when she was scared of the band. That's what I'm proudest of." He never mentioned the rank. Gopika leaned her head on his shoulder.

qa.q: What did Yogesh tell every uncle at the wedding?
What does Gopika's question to her father show she was worried about?
qa.a: It shows she worried his love depended on her marks and brilliance.

qa.q: What turning point did Yogesh choose after hearing her question?
qa.a: He took her for chai and praised her kindness to her cousin, not mentioning the rank at all.

qa.q: What was the wedding like for Gopika while Yogesh boasted?
qa.a: She smiled until her cheeks hurt, feeling shown off for her marks rather than just being herself.

grounding: It shows a proud father pushing achievement, a daughter who feels loved only for brilliance, and how valuing her beyond ability comforts her.
